Empowering Learners & Changing Lives

A snapshot overview of data that shows the collective impact of programs and services of the Maine Department of Education's Office of Workforce & Innovative Pathways (WDIP) in expanding learning opportunities for students and supporting Maine's workforce goals.

Download WDIP Data Flyer PDF

Workforce Resources for Schools & Students

Are you looking for a way to support students looking to work or explore career options?

  • Career Exploration - The Maine Department of Labor, Center for Workforce Research and Information produces long-term employment projections by occupation at the statewide and regional areas. These projections identify growing/declining jobs based on demographic, industrial, and technological trends, and predictions. We’ve used these projections to create a discovery dashboard for students and jobseekers to explore the many career options available to them, what the future looks like for occupations in Maine, and the educational/training requirements that are often necessary to pursue a desired career path. For the best user experience, we recommend using a computer or tablet. (Center for Workforce Research & Information)

  • Maine Department of Labor - The Maine Department of Labor is working to ensure that staff, counselors, and teachers have the tools they need to empower their students as they enter the world of work and ensure that students and their families know their rights and available resources.

decisions.label: Put the card titles on one level
decisions.why: 2 card titles are written at a level copied from an example rather than chosen — h5 on a page whose sections are h2. Only the number changes.

decisions.label: Let very uneven cards find their own height
decisions.why: 1 row pairs a short card with one holding nearly three times as much. Equal heights stretch the short one and the difference reads as a hole, so these are allowed to sit at the height of what is in them.

decisions.label: Give the cards the width their content needs
decisions.why: 1 row holds two cards of very different weight in equal halves, and cards in a row are the same height — so the short one is stretched and the difference shows as empty space. 3.4× — 1156 characters beside 336. Only the column widths change.

decisions.label: Put the buttons on the house style
decisions.why: 1 button uses a Bootstrap variant rather than btn-info, so the same kind of action is drawn three different ways across the site. Only the class changes.

decisions.label: Drop the dash once the link is set apart
decisions.why: 2 of those items separate the link from its description with a dash. The link is now set in the display face at a larger size with a chevron after it, so the dash marks a boundary that is already unmistakable. Only the separator is removed — no word changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 2 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Set a job title the way the rest of the site does
decisions.why: 1 job title sits in plain text under the person's name, where 186 elsewhere on the site are in italics — so the same contact block is drawn two ways depending on the page, and the title runs into the name above it. The standard here is the site's own, not a preference: two thirds of these blocks already do it. No word changes.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
